width_rule: wg_width set to single_mode_width_um=1.0; all feature widths remain >= min_feature_um=0.4.
physics_rule: FSR_nm = wavelength_um^2 * 1000 / (n_g * delta_length_um); at 1.55 um and 8.0 nm target, delta_length_target_um = 300.3125 / n_g.

iterations.reasoning: Initial SiN evaluation with wg_width=1.0 shows the recreated 10.5 um imbalance is far too short. Since FSR=lambda^2/(n_g*delta_L), the lower SiN group index requires a larger path imbalance than SOI: delta_L=300.3125/2.0212899446487427=148.5746766786533 um. The longer lower arm is generated from gf.Path geometry controlled by delta_length, so I will set delta_length to this target.

The computed SiN imbalance converged. The measured gf.Path imbalance is 148.574 um after path quantization; substituting it into FSR=lambda^2/(n_g*delta_L) gives 8.00003643591225 nm, safely inside the 2% tolerance. No further geometry move is needed.

final_raster.note: Rasterized optimized GDS against the original image calibration after spec convergence; IoU drop is expected because the lower arm was lengthened to meet FSR.
